title: Spatial organization of HPV-associated immune programs across tissue compartments in oropharyngeal cancer

analysis.research_question_and_background: HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) is characterized by a distinct immune microenvironment, but the biological significance of immune-related transcriptional programs may vary based on their spatial localization.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A TCGA-OPSCC cohort comprising 77 tumors (51 HPV-positive and 26 HPV-negative) was analyzed, alongside spatial transcriptomic profiling in six OPC patients (four HPV-positive and two HPV-negative) and an independent microarray cohort of 23 HPV-positive and four HPV-negative cases of tumor-free palatine tonsillar tissue.
analysis.methods: Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) was used to evaluate immune-related transcriptional programs in the TCGA-OPSCC cohort. Spatial transcriptomic profiling using GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiling was conducted in lymphoid follicular regions (LFRs) and tumor tissue regions (TTRs) from six OPC patients, with patient as the primary experimental unit. Eight prespecified immune- and metabolism-related transcriptional programs were assessed, including cell-type deconvolution and overall survival analyses.
analysis.main_results: In TCGA-OPSCC, all five immune-related programs were higher in HPV-positive tumors, and four remained significantly associated with HPV-positive status after adjustment for clinicopathological covariates and FDR correction. In GeoMx analyses, all five immune-related programs were higher in LFRs than in TTRs in all six patients, whereas Estrogen Response Early and Estrogen Response Late were higher in TTRs (BH-FDR = 0.0357 for each program). Bile Acid Metabolism showed no consistent compartment-specific difference. HPV-associated differences within individual GeoMx compartments and HPV-by-compartment interactions were not statistically significant after FDR correction.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HPV-associated immune transcriptional programs identified in bulk OPC show consistent spatial organization across lymphoid follicular and tumor tissue compartments, with the most robust spatial feature being within-patient compartmentalization between LFRs and TTRs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings emphasize the importance of anatomical context when interpreting transcriptional programs in OPC, which may inform more precise surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence for HPV-associated differences within individual spatial compartments was limited, and HPV-associated differences within GeoMx compartments were not statistically significant after FDR correction, suggesting the need for further studies with larger sample sizes and more detailed spatial analyses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the spatial organization of HPV-associated immune transcriptional programs in oropharyngeal cancer (OPC). It finds that immune-related programs are consistently higher in HPV-positive tumors compared to HPV-negative ones, with significant associations remaining after statistical adjustments. Spatial transcriptomic profiling reveals that immune programs are more active in lymphoid follicular regions (LFRs) than in tumor tissue regions (TTRs) across all six patients, while estrogen response programs are more prevalent in TTRs. However, HPV-associated differences within individual compartments and interactions between HPV and compartments are not statistically significant after FDR correction. The study highlights the importance of anatomical context in interpreting transcriptional programs in OPC, which may have implications for targeted surveillance and treatment strategies. The findings are based on a TCGA-OPSCC cohort and independent microarray analyses, but the evidence for compartment-specific HPV differences is limited, suggesting the need for further research.
